newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African diesel price set to be cut by 19 cts/ltr.
newsitem.headline: S.African diesel price set to be cut by 19 cts/ltr.

text.p: South Africa's diesel price is expected to be cut by 19 cents a litre from March to its lowest level since October last year, a reduction which economists say holds positive implications for inflation.
According to latest Central Energy Fund (CEF) statistics, South Africa recorded an over-recovery of 19.537 cents in its diesel price this month.

Petrol, which has registered an over-recovery of 4.54 cents so far this month as a result of a stronger rand and lower international oil prices, is expected to be reduced by four to five cents a litre.

South African diesel prices have traditionally been set at a lower price than petrol, but this trend was reversed last year because of an upgrade to European refineries where environmental laws called for a reduction in sulphur content.
"At the same time there was high growth of imports of diesel into China and India because of economic growth," E.W Balderson economist Mike Schussler said.
As a result, diesel prices rose sharply last year and had moved in line with domestic petrol prices. Both currently cost 223 cents per litre.
However, a recent slowdown in Chinese imports by as much as 50 percent had resulted in international prices moving lower in recent weeks.

"The Chinese may have expected trouble in China with the possible death of Deng Xiaoping because all of a sudden just before the Chinese New Year they reduced their buying by about 50 percent," Schussler said.
Another reason could be demand for heating fuel. "They could also have built up their stocks because of an expected cold winter," Schussler said.
The result was that Chinese diesel stocks were probably quite high at the moment, which had led to lower demand, Schussler said.
A CEF official said that while a reduction in the prices could be expected, the exact amount would depend on whether government decided to increase levies, the fuel tax or margins.
If the diesel price is cut by 19 cents, however, it would reduce it to its lowest level since October 2 last year, when a litre cost 204 cents.
One economist, who asked not to be named, said the reduction in petrol and diesel prices would probably result in a 0.2 percent reduction in the consumer price index in March.
"On the producer price index it will probably have a slightly bigger impact," the economist said, "because on the industrial side diesel is a little bit more important than petrol."

Schussler estimated that the direct and indirect effects of a 19 cent cut in the diesel price could result in producer inflation being reduced by as much as one percent if the lower price was maintained throughout the year.
Because of recent price increases, he said, diesel prices made up about 30 percent of transport costs for road freight.
"But it is probably moving back to its long-term moving average of about 27 percent of these costs," Schussler said.
CEF will announce the price cuts on Friday morning.
